newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - New Australia gold area said to need big find.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - New Australia gold area said to need big find.

text.p: Resolute Samantha Ltd believed a 200-300,000 ounce gold reserve would be needed to justify a mine operation in South Australia's hot new gold region, the Gawler Craton, exploration director Ross Kennedy said on Monday.
Kennedy said the costs of establishing infrastructure in the underexplored region would require greater reserves than, for example, Kalgoorlie where 150,000 mineable ounces were feasible.
"When you do the economic modelling, we will need somewhere between 200-300,000 ounces," he told a conference here on prospects for the Gawler Craton.

Ric Horn from the state's Department of Mines and Energy, which unveiled the Gawler Craton with a 1992 aeromagnetic survey, said exploration spending there was expected to rise to more than A$15 million in 1996 from A$10 million last year.
More than 32 companies now held more than 70 exploration licences and licence applications covering 80 percent of the western portion of the Craton, he said.

The Resolute Samantha/Dominion Mining Ltd joint venture prospect of Challenger remains the most exciting to date, having recorded intersections of 16 metres at 7.6 grams per tonne and 16 metres at 6.7 g/t.
Kennedy said the venture would begin reverse circulation and diamond drilling in some of the deeper holes at Challenger in December to obtain samples of the metallurgy.
Resolute believed it could achieve 90 percent recovery of gold in the ore at Challenger and was moving on the prospect "as fast as we can," he later told Reuters.

The joint venture had covered about 50 percent of its total 22,000 square km Gawler acreage with calcrete sampling, and would spend about A$5 million in the next twelve months on further exploration work, he said.

Also at the conference, junior explorer Minotaur Gold Ltd said it was proposing to place 4.4 million shares to raise an additional A$1.32 million, which would increase its cash in hand to A$4.2 million.

Managing director Derek Carter said he expected to announce later this week a joint venture agreement with a major mining company for the Hermitage Creek copper-gold prospect on the eastern edge of the Craton, where a discrete gravity anomaly had been outlined.
Helix Resources NL said it was awaiting the result of reverse circulation drilling over the next few months at its Tunkilia prospect at Lake Everard.
Lawyer Ewan Vickery told the conference there currently were seven native title claims on the Gawler Craton region, including offshore areas, a number of which were overlapping.
He said developers should expect to wait a minimum 12 month period to obtain a mining lease for properites affected by native title, while ready access could be gained for exploration.
